facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
no breast symptoms
a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast
no discrete abnormality corresponding to the mammographic finding
a tomosynthesis-guided vacuum-assisted biopsy of the right inner breast was performed
yielding 12 core specimens
marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils
with lymphocytes and plasma cells and no granulomata
no history of urticaria, asthma, angioedema, or pruritus except for seasonal allergic rhinitis
Peripheral blood eosinophil levels were within the normal range
Hypereosinophilic syndrome was excluded from consideration
asymptomatic

concepts.why: The presence of lymphocytes and plasma cells in the inflammatory infiltrate supports this diagnosis, although the lack of associated allergic symptoms is unusual.

support_spans: a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast
marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils
contradict_spans: no discrete abnormality corresponding to the mammographic finding
concepts.why: The presence of a developing asymmetry and a mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate supports this diagnosis, although the lack of associated diabetes is not mentioned.

support_spans: marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils
with lymphocytes and plasma cells and no granulomata
contradict_spans: no history of urticaria, asthma, angioedema, or pruritus except for seasonal allergic rhinitis
concepts.why: The presence of a mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate with eosinophils, lymphocytes, and plasma cells supports this diagnosis, although the lack of associated IgG4-related disease symptoms is unusual.

rationales.F07: Eosinophilic mastitis is more likely due to the presence of eosinophils in the biopsy specimen.
rationales.F08: The presence of lymphocytes and plasma cells, but no granulomata, makes Idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis less likely.
rationales.F10: Normal peripheral blood eosinophil levels decrease the likelihood of Hypereosinophilic syndrome and Eosinophilic mastitis.
rationales.F11: The exclusion of Hypereosinophilic syndrome decreases the likelihood of Eosinophilic mastitis.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of a marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils specifically supports Eosinophilic mastitis, despite normal peripheral blood eosinophil levels.
